firstTimers.name: Sham Foam Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Sham Foam's document is a Rs 4,048 lakh SME IPO prospectus, not an earnings call: FY26 revenue Rs 9,231.92 lakh, PAT Rs 865.06 lakh, and capacity utilisation rising to 87.62% with Rs 1,471.65 lakh of proceeds earmarked for expansion.

firstTimers.name: Veegaland Developers Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Kerala residential developer posts Q2 revenue up 28.7% to INR106.3 cr and PAT up 92%, but the read is mostly demand and margin mix; no supply-side capacity signal, and ~INR500 cr of unrecognised revenue plus ~INR1,080 cr order book gives visibility.

firstTimers.name: Tonbo Imaging India Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “Since this is our first call, I'd like to take this opportunity to introduce the company and set the context”
firstTimers.thesis: Tonbo's first post-listing call: H1 FY27 revenue INR219 crore with Q2 at INR183 crore, but no numeric guidance; order book INR250 crore and INR408 crore under negotiation support a stronger H2, with the company asking to be judged annually.

firstTimers.name: Prabha Energy Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “Thank you for joining for the maiden call of Prabha Energy Limited”
firstTimers.thesis: Maiden call from a pre-revenue CBM player: gas sales only ~20,000 cubic metres/day via cascades, with volumes contingent on pipeline connectivity by Jan and Mar 2027 and peak only in FY29; capex of 500 crore pending.

firstTimers.name: Gujarat Kidney and Super Speciality Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Asset-light hospital roll-up with H1 FY27 revenue INR72.4 cr (+157% YoY) but thin operating cash flow (~INR0.4 cr vs PAT INR11.9 cr); no numeric guidance and no supply-side capacity data.

firstTimers.name: Augmont Enterprises Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “On behalf of Augmont Enterprises Limited, it gives me great pleasure to welcome you to the company's first earnings conference call following its listing”
firstTimers.thesis: Augmont's Q2 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.85 Cr (2.5x YoY) on scrap-led margins, but revenue fell 32% in enterprise and management gave no numeric guidance; capacity is 20 delivery centres with 10 more planned.

firstTimers.name: Lumino Industries Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Lumino's H1 FY27 manufacturing utilisation is only about 60-62% on 40,000 MT, with volumes down to 13,781 MT from 15,800 MT, while the EPC-heavy order book (INR2,885 cr) and a 75,000 MT expansion add capacity ahead of demand.

firstTimers.name: Moneyview Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “Since this is our first call, I will spend a few minutes introducing Moneyview and then take you through the quarter and our outlook”
firstTimers.thesis: Digital lender with capital-light LSP model; Q2 PAT INR 201 crores (+16% QoQ), FY27 PAT guided above INR 800 crores, credit cost 4.9% annualised held inside 5% ceiling; supply-side metrics not applicable.

firstTimers.name: Atharva Poly-Plast Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Engineering-led polymer molder at 67% utilisation with 88% target and no capex until FY28-29; H1 revenue +77.5% YoY but EBITDA margin 20.3% vs 11.5% in H2, with management blaming a one-month polymer pass-through lag.

firstTimers.name: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Exchange franchise is strong: Q2 FY27 transaction charges up 9% to ₹3,035 crore with 92% cash share, but cash ADT fell 13% QoQ and equity futures ADT down 11.7% YoY on tax changes.

firstTimers.name: Robokidz Eduventures Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “This is our first call following our listing on BSE SME platform and I'm happy to have this opportunity to interact with all of you and share more about our business performance and the direction in which we are moving”
firstTimers.thesis: Small-cap education-lab operator with H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin ~22.9% and receivables-driven working capital (~INR73 cr vs INR60 cr H1 revenue), with management admitting it may need external capital in FY28.

firstTimers.name: Sahajanand Medical Technologies Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Record Q2 with revenue up 24.7% to ~INR373 cr and EBITDA up 36.6%, but supply-side evidence is mixed: Surat PTCA utilisation fell and Telangana DES sits at 20%, while capex is held at ~INR70 cr for FY27-28.

firstTimers.name: GSPL Transmission Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Regulated gas pipeline operator with flat H1 profit (PAT +1%) and a INR 3,500 crore expansion mostly back-ended to FY28; volumes up 12% YoY on a re-based contractual metric, with subsidiaries GIGL and GITL still loss-making.

firstTimers.name: Manipal Payment and Identity Solutions Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: H1 FY27 revenue up 40% to INR 849 crore with core up 23% and emerging up 92%, but operational EBITDA margin fell to 30.1% and working capital days rose to 96; supply-side read is capacity at 75-80% utilisation with INR 240 crore capex funded from IPO.

firstTimers.name: Shree Vasu Logistics Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Strong H1 FY27 print (revenue +37% to Rs145cr, PAT 8.4cr from 3.1cr) but no supply-side disclosure: no capacity, utilisation or pricing data, and the call was thin with an unidentified caller and retail questioners.

firstTimers.name: Gamco Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: A diversified NBFC-turned-asset holder: H1 FY27 revenue up 79% to INR254 crores with Q2 EBITDA margin only 9%, funded by rising borrowings (D/E 1.6x) and development-stage real estate, hospitality and warehousing with no capacity-discipline evidence.

firstTimers.name: Rajputana Stainless Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “Good afternoon everyone and welcome to Ra jputana Stainless Limited's maiden earnings call to discuss Q2 and H1 FY27 financial performance”
firstTimers.thesis: Capacity fully utilised (~99%) with a 25% melt expansion to 60,000 t slated for Q4 FY27, funded internally, while H1 operating cash flow of ~INR4.5 cr lagged PAT of INR43.9 cr as receivables rose.

firstTimers.thesis: FY26 revenue Rs 318 cr (+50%) with EBITDA margin ~10%, but H2 margins fell on raw-material inflation; manufacturing only 23% of revenue and the new polymer plant is still in teething trials.

firstTimers.name: Novus Loyalty Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “As this marks the company's first earnings call following its listing, today's interaction is an important milestone in its journey toward building long -term value and strengthening engagement with the investor community”
firstTimers.thesis: Loyalty platform FY26 revenue ~127 Cr (+22%), EBITDA margin 9.68%, PAT margin 7.29%; management gives no numeric FY27 guidance beyond international revenue doubling and 15-20% India growth, with a thin, promotional Q&A.

firstTimers.name: Kiaasa Retail Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Kiaasa is a small SME-listed ethnic-wear EBO roll-out story with FY26 revenue of Rs134.63 cr and EBITDA margin of 17.8%, but no supply-side evidence (capacity, utilisation, pricing) and a 35% revenue CAGR vision to FY30 that management did not tie to capex.

firstTimers.name: Star Imaging And Path Lab Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Diagnostics operator with revenue up only 6% to INR88.5 crore in FY26 after guiding 30-35%; FY27 growth now guided at 25-30% with capex of INR20-25 crore and no new debt, but execution delays undercut credibility.

firstTimers.name: Workmates Core2Cloud Solution Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Cloud/AI services firm guides FY27 revenue to INR 210 cr (+45%) with INR 190 cr visibility, but FY26 margins fell (EBITDA 16.2% vs 17.7%) and no supply-side capacity data is given.

firstTimers.name: Om Power Transmission Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: Transcript: “Good evening and thank yo u for taking the time out to join us in the maiden Earnings Conference Call of Om Power T ransmission Limited”
firstTimers.thesis: Maiden call of a T&D EPC: FY26 revenue INR 449 crore (+61%), order book INR 621 crore (book-to-bill 1.38x), EBITDA margin steady at 12.7%, with management guiding 50% growth in FY27 and 12-13% EBITDA margin.

firstTimers.name: Nukleus Office Solutions Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Flex-workspace operator guiding to ~10 lakh sq ft operational by FY27 end (from ~3.5 lakh), but gave no revenue numbers, and fixed assets up 160% with debt-funded expansion and thin disclosure quality.

firstTimers.name: Creative Newtech Ltd
firstTimers.evidence: No earnings call transcript or analyst / investor meet filing on BSE from 2019 until this call
firstTimers.thesis: Creative Newtech is a market-entry distributor with a rising brand mix; Q4 margins flattered by Make-in-India mix, while receivables jumped to ~20% of turnover and Middle East freight shock threatens brand sales.
